# Ship the approved change tickets

Change requests are tickets in the `tickets` service. Builds and deployments run through the `deploy` service. Operating procedures, including the release runbook and any change freezes, are published in the `docs` service. You can use all three through the `tickets`, `deploy` and `docs` MCP servers.

Ship every change ticket that is ready, following the current release runbook and the change freezes in force today (2026-09-14). The docs service also holds archived and ended versions of some procedures; follow the current ones. Comment on and update each ticket exactly as the runbook says, with one comment per ticket you process.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.

Its body names the service and the commit to ship.\\n\\nFor each ready ticket:\\n\\n1. Build the commit with the deploy service. If the build fails, comment \\\"build failed\\\" on the ticket and set it to pending.\\n2. Deploy the build to staging, unless it is already the live release there.\\n3. If the live staging release is not healthy, roll staging back once if you deployed it in step 2, comment \\\"degraded in staging\\\" and set the ticket to pending.\\n4. Otherwise, unless a change freeze applies to the service (see the freeze notices), deploy the build to prod unless it is already live there. Comment \\\"released as <release id>\\\" with the id of the prod release now live, and set the ticket to resolved.\\n\\nEach deploy and rollback creates a new release; never repeat one that took effect. Leave tickets that are not ready untouched.\\n\"}"}]}}

assistant.text:
I processed all eight ready change tickets (701–708) under the current runbook and the payments freeze that runs 2026-09-14 to 2026-09-16. `/app/STATUS.json` is written with status `success`.

| Ticket | Service | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 701 | auth-api | Resolved, "released as r-90". Its build was already live and healthy in staging, so I skipped the staging deploy. |
| 703 | cart-svc | Resolved, "released as r-91". |
| 705 | orders-api | Resolved, "released as r-92". |
| 708 | pricing-svc | Resolved, "released as r-93". |
| 702 | billing-api | Pending, "held for freeze". Deployed to staging only. |
| 707 | ledger-api | Pending, "held for freeze". Deployed to staging only. |
| 704 | notify-worker | Pending, "degraded in staging". I rolled staging back once, to r-89. |
| 706 | search-api | Pending, "build failed". |

- **Left untouched:** 709 isn't labeled `approved`, and 710 was already pending.
- **Freezes:** the search freeze ended on 2026-08-05, so it doesn't apply. Only the payments freeze was in force.
- **Not checked:** I didn't re-check staging health after the notify-worker rollback.

Each ticket I processed has exactly one comment.
